Carlos — thanks for the note and congrats on the pilot moving to production. High level options we commonly recommend: 

1) Staged top-up (preferred) — Add a temporary burst bucket that sits alongside your committed units for the remainder of the contract. Units draw from burst first; any sustained uplift above N% gets converted to committed units at renewal with a blended rate. This preserves current renewal pricing while giving flexibility.

2) Mid-contract uplift amendment — Amend the contract now with an uplift and partial annualization. You commit to X additional units for the remainder of term, billed pro-rata, with a reduced uplift discount vs. full renewal.

3) Pilot co-term carve-in — Create a short-term pilot SKU that we invoice separately until your renewal, then co-term and annualize the pilot consumption at renewal with a guaranteed conversion discount. Minimizes procurement churn but requires a one-time amendment and a small admin fee.

I've attached a short worksheet with numbers and a draft amendment template to show the billing mechanics (Graystone_Renewal_Options_v1.pdf and SOW-Topup-Appendix.xlsx).

Preliminary recommendation: staged top-up + fair-share conversion at renewal (option 1). It keeps your per-token economics close to current rates and avoids double invoicing. If procurement needs a single invoice now, option 3 is workable — we'll need PO details and a quick approval from finance.

Next steps I propose:
- I update the worksheet with your expected Q4 token estimates (can you confirm the projected 25% in absolute tokens?)
- Prioyom (cc) will confirm the exact discount bands we can offer for partial annualization and whether we can waive the admin fee for strategic customers.
- I can produce a DocuSign amendment that co-terms the pilot into the renewal if you choose option 3.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to run the numbers.
